jabal-amil.s: Jabal Amil is a region in southern Lebanon with a long tradition of Shia scholarship. The Safavid Empire imported Arab Shia scholars from Jabal Amil and Bahrain to help convert Iran to Twelver Shia Islam.

jacques-cartier.s: Jacques Cartier was a French explorer who made voyages to North America from 1534. He explored the Gulf of St.

jadwiga-of-poland.s: Jadwiga was crowned ruler of Poland in the late fourteenth century. Under the Union of Krewo of 1385 she married the Lithuanian grand duke Jogaila, who accepted Latin Christianity and became King Władysław II Jagiełło.

jafari-school.s: The Ja'fari school is the main school of Twelver Shia Islamic jurisprudence, named after the imam Ja'far al-Sadiq. In 1736 Nader Shah proposed that it be recognised as a fifth school of law alongside the four Sunni schools.

jagiellonian-dynasty.s: The Jagiellonian dynasty was a royal house that ruled Poland, Lithuania and at times Bohemia and Hungary from the late fourteenth to the late sixteenth century. It began with Jogaila's marriage to Jadwiga in 1386.

jagir.s: A jagir was an assignment of land revenue to an official or military commander in South Asia, typically in return for service. In the Mughal Empire jagirs supported the mansabdars, and were usually transferable rather than hereditary.

jalali-calendar.s: The Jalali calendar is a solar calendar introduced in the late eleventh century under the Seljuk sultan Malik Shah, with the participation of the mathematician Omar Khayyam. It was more accurate than the contemporary Julian calendar.

jalayirid-sultanate.s: The Jalayirid Sultanate was a Mongol-descended dynasty that ruled Iraq and western Iran in the fourteenth century. It emerged from the fragmentation of the Ilkhanate after the death of Abu Sa'id in 1335.

jamaica.s: Jamaica is a Caribbean island that was a British colony from the seventeenth century until 1962, with a plantation economy based on enslaved labour. It adopted the Westminster parliamentary model inherited from the British Empire.

jamestown.s: Jamestown was an English settlement in Virginia founded in 1607. It was the first permanent English colony in North America.

jami.s: Jami was a fifteenth-century Persian poet and Sufi scholar, active in Herat. He is regarded as one of the last great classical Persian poets.

jami-al-tawarikh.s: Jami' al-Tawarikh, or Compendium of Chronicles, is a universal history compiled by Rashid al-Din, vizier of the Ilkhanate, in the early fourteenth century. It covers the Mongols and many other peoples of Eurasia and was richly illustrated.

jan-iii-sobieski.s: Jan III Sobieski was King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth in the late seventeenth century and an accomplished military commander. In 1683 he led the relief army that defeated the Ottoman siege of Vienna.

jan-pieterszoon-coen.s: Jan Pieterszoon Coen was an officer and Governor-General of the Dutch East India Company in the early seventeenth century. He founded Batavia on Java in 1619 as the company's headquarters.

janissaries.s: The Janissaries were the elite infantry corps of the Ottoman Empire, originally recruited from Christian boys through the devshirme system. They became one of the first standing armies in Europe to use firearms on a large scale.

japan.s: Japan is an island nation in East Asia. It absorbed many influences from the Tang Dynasty and resisted the invasions of the Yuan Dynasty, was unified under the Tokugawa Shogunate, and traded with Portuguese and Dutch merchants.

japanese-invasion-of-the-dutch-east-indi.n: Japanese invasion of the Dutch East Indies
japanese-invasion-of-the-dutch-east-indi.s: The Japanese invasion of the Dutch East Indies was a campaign of 1941–1942 in which Japanese forces conquered the Dutch colonial territories in present-day Indonesia, seeking their oil and other resources. The Allied naval forces were defeated in the Battle of the Java Sea.

japanese-tea-ceremony.s: The Japanese tea ceremony is a ritual preparation and serving of powdered green tea, shaped by Zen Buddhist ideals of simplicity and harmony. It was refined by masters such as Sen no Rikyū in the sixteenth century.

japonisme.s: Japonisme was the fashion for Japanese art and design in Europe and America in the later nineteenth century, after Japan opened to the West. Japanese woodblock prints influenced Impressionism, Post-Impressionism and Art Nouveau.

java.s: Java is a densely populated island in Indonesia. It was the heartland of the Majapahit Empire and an important rival or part of the Srivijaya sphere.

java-sea.s: The Java Sea is a shallow sea between Java, Borneo and Sumatra in Indonesia. It was a key maritime trade route used by the Srivijaya and Majapahit empires.

jawhar-al-siqilli.s: Jawhar al-Siqilli was a Fatimid general of Sicilian or slave origin. In 969 CE he led the conquest of Egypt for the Fatimid Caliphate and founded the new city of Cairo.

jayavarman-ii.s: Jayavarman II was a Khmer ruler who in 802 CE proclaimed himself universal monarch, or chakravartin, in a ceremony declaring independence from Java. His reign is traditionally regarded as the foundation of the Khmer Empire.

jayavarman-vii.s: Jayavarman VII was a Khmer king of the late twelfth and early thirteenth century. He drove out Cham invaders who had sacked Angkor and expanded the empire to its greatest extent.

jean-baptiste-colbert.s: Jean-Baptiste Colbert was a minister of Louis XIV of France who directed finance, commerce and the navy. He promoted mercantilist policies, trading companies and colonial development, and built up the French navy.

jean-baptiste-ventura.s: Jean-Baptiste Ventura was an Italian former officer of Napoleon's armies who entered the service of Ranjit Singh. With other European officers he helped train Sikh infantry along European lines.

jean-francois-allard.s: Jean-François Allard was a French former officer of Napoleon's armies who entered the service of Ranjit Singh. He organised and trained cavalry units of the Sikh army on European lines.

jean-jacques-dessalines.s: Jean-Jacques Dessalines was a leader of the Haitian Revolution. After the defeat of the French expedition, he declared the independence of Haiti in 1804 and became its first ruler.

jehoiachin.s: Jehoiachin was a king of Judah who surrendered Jerusalem to Nebuchadnezzar II in 597 BCE. He was deported to Babylon with the Judean elite.

jeronimos-monastery.s: The Jerónimos Monastery is a monastery in Lisbon built from the early sixteenth century in the ornate Manueline style. Its construction was funded by revenues from the spice trade.

jerusalem.s: Jerusalem is an ancient city in the Levant, sacred to Judaism, Christianity and Islam. It was destroyed by the Chaldean Empire, restored under the Achaemenid Empire, and taken by the Sasanian Empire in the seventh century.

jesuits.s: The Jesuits, or Society of Jesus, are a Catholic religious order founded in 1540. They were leading missionaries in Asia, Africa and the Americas.

jews.s: The Jews are a people and religious community descended from the ancient Israelites. Jewish communities lived in many empires, often as protected minorities.

jezzailchi.s: Jezzailchis were soldiers armed with the jezail, a long-barrelled musket used in Iran, Afghanistan and Central Asia. Nader Shah employed mounted infantry armed with firearms who could dismount to deliver accurate musket fire and then remount for pursuit.

jhelum.s: The Jhelum is one of the five rivers of the Punjab, flowing from Kashmir into present-day Pakistan. With the Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, it sustained the intensive agriculture of the region.

jiaozi.s: Jiaozi was a form of paper money that first appeared in Sichuan in the early eleventh century, initially issued by merchants and later taken over by the government. It is generally regarded as the world's first government-issued paper currency.

jiedushi.s: Jiedushi were military governors of the Tang Dynasty, originally appointed to command frontier armies. Over time they gained control of civil administration, taxation and troops in their regions.

jihad.s: Jihad is an Islamic term meaning struggle or striving, which can refer to spiritual effort or to armed struggle in defence or expansion of the faith. Armed jihad was a central theme in the founding of the Sokoto Caliphate and in Saladin's wars against the crusaders in the…

jinchuan-campaigns.s: The Jinchuan campaigns were military expeditions of the Qing Empire in the eighteenth century against the Jinchuan chieftaincies in the mountains of western Sichuan. Fought in difficult terrain against fortified stone towers, they proved extremely costly.

jingkang-incident.s: The Jingkang incident was the capture of the Northern Song capital Kaifeng by Jurchen Jin forces in 1127, in which the retired emperor Huizong and the reigning emperor Qinzong were taken captive. The Song court re-established itself in the south.

jinshi.s: Jinshi was the highest degree in the Chinese imperial examination system, awarded to candidates who passed the metropolitan and palace examinations. Holders were eligible for senior posts in the bureaucracy.

jizya.s: Jizya was a tax levied in Islamic states on non-Muslim subjects, the dhimmi, in return for protection and exemption from military service. It was established in the Rashidun Caliphate and continued in the Umayyad Caliphate, where it was an important source of revenue.

joao-afonso-de-aveiro.s: João Afonso de Aveiro was a Portuguese explorer who reached the kingdom of Benin in the 1480s. His visit led to formal diplomatic and commercial relations between Portugal and Benin under Oba Ozolua.

johann-martin-honigberger.s: Johann Martin Honigberger was a physician from Transylvania who served at the court of Ranjit Singh in Lahore. He later wrote a memoir, Thirty-five Years in the East.

johannes-gutenberg.s: Johannes Gutenberg was a fifteenth-century German craftsman who developed printing with movable metal type in Europe. His press transformed the spread of knowledge in Europe.

johannes-van-den-bosch.s: Johannes van den Bosch was a Dutch Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies. In 1830 he introduced the Cultivation System in Java, which forced peasants to devote part of their land or labour to export crops for the colonial government.

john-i-of-portugal.s: John I of Portugal was the founder of the House of Aviz, who secured the throne after a succession crisis in the late fourteenth century. His reign confirmed Portuguese independence from Castile.

john-ii-of-portugal.s: John II of Portugal was a king of the late fifteenth century who vigorously promoted exploration along the African coast. During his reign Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope, and he negotiated the Treaty of Tordesillas with Spain.

john-v-of-portugal.s: John V of Portugal was a king of the first half of the eighteenth century. Gold and diamonds discovered in Brazil funded his extravagant court culture and building projects.

johor.s: Johor is a state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, which became the seat of a Malay sultanate after the fall of Malacca. Like Malacca, Penang and Singapore, it functioned as a commercial entrepôt.

joint-stock-company.s: A joint-stock company is a business owned by shareholders who invest capital and share in its profits and losses. The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, was an early and influential example with publicly traded shares.

jolof-empire.s: The Jolof Empire was a Wolof state in present-day Senegal that dominated the region from the fourteenth to the sixteenth century. It was made up of a confederation of kingdoms under the Buurba Jolof.

jong-ship.s: The jong was a large ocean-going ship of the Javanese and Malay world, capable of carrying large crews and cargoes. Majapahit's naval forces used such ships to transport troops, horses and supplies across the archipelago.

josiah-harlan.s: Josiah Harlan was an American adventurer who travelled to Afghanistan and the Punjab in the early nineteenth century. He was among the foreign officers employed by Ranjit Singh.

judaea.s: Judaea was the region of the southern Levant centred on Jerusalem, the land of the Jewish people in antiquity. Under the Seleucid Empire its Jewish communities initially kept their ancestral law.

judah.s: Judah was an ancient kingdom in the southern Levant with its capital at Jerusalem. It was conquered by the Chaldean Empire under Nebuchadnezzar II.

judaism.s: Judaism is the monotheistic religion of the Jewish people, based on the Hebrew Bible and rabbinic tradition. Its history was shaped by the Assyrian and Chaldean conquests, the Achaemenid restoration and the conflict with the Seleucid Empire.

judar-pasha.s: Judar Pasha was a commander in the service of the Saadi sultan of Morocco, of Spanish origin. In 1591 he led a Moroccan army of about 4,000 soldiers across the Sahara and defeated the Songhai at the Battle of Tondibi using firearms.

jugol.s: The Jugol is the defensive wall of the city of Harar in eastern Ethiopia. It was built under Nur ibn Mujahid in the mid-sixteenth century, after the death of Imam Ahmad.

julian-emperor.s: Julian was a Roman emperor of the fourth century CE, known for attempting to restore traditional paganism. He led a major expedition against Persia but died in the campaign in 363 CE.

julian-calendar.s: The Julian calendar is a solar calendar introduced by Julius Caesar in 46 BCE, with a leap year every four years. It remained the standard calendar in Europe until the Gregorian reform.

julius-caesar.s: Julius Caesar was a Roman general and statesman whose victory in civil war made him dictator, before his assassination in 44 BCE. His intervention in Egypt supported Cleopatra VII, and their relationship drew the Ptolemaic Empire into Roman politics.

july-crisis.s: The July Crisis was the diplomatic crisis of 1914 following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo. Austria-Hungary issued an ultimatum to Serbia, and alliances drew the great powers into the First World War.

jurchen-jin-dynasty.s: The Jurchen Jin dynasty ruled northern China from 1115 until 1234. It destroyed the Liao and captured the Song capital Kaifeng in 1127.

jurchens.s: The Jurchens were a Tungusic people of Manchuria. In the twelfth century they founded the Jin dynasty, which conquered northern China from the Song Dynasty.

jury-trial.s: Jury trial is a legal procedure in which a panel of citizens decides the facts of a case. In the Russian Empire, Alexander II's Judicial Reform of 1864 introduced trial by jury along with independent courts and adversarial procedure.

justin-i.s: Justin I was a Byzantine emperor of the early sixth century, uncle of Justinian I. According to the site, a major Aksumite naval expedition across the Red Sea was undertaken at his request.

justinian-i.s: Justinian I was a Byzantine emperor of the sixth century CE. He ordered the codification of Roman law later known as the Corpus Juris Civilis, built the Hagia Sophia and reconquered parts of the western Mediterranean.
